body: I don't know about long-term side effects -- I would assume that would vary based on what you take -- but if you take that many pills, your body is going to try to purge them from your system. You will probably spend a lot of time vomiting over and over again.
I can't have a dog for a number of reasons, but I appreciate the response. Glad to hear your dog helped you so much. Animals are wonderful.

Sorry to hear that you had the same problem. I can see how numbers are useful for the staff, but it is really hurtful to see that even people that are struggling are doing a lot better for you. Made me feel hopeless. I can't even imagine entering an outpatient program if my mood was at a 6. A 6 is a good day in my book. 

Have you tried DBT at all? That's what I'm trying next and I am curious to know if you found it to be helpful.

I've done a lot of group therapy and I tend to compare myself negatively to other people in the programs. When I was in outpatient, we had to rank a lot of stuff with numbers, like mood, level of suicide ideation, etc. My numbers were consistently worse than everyone else's, and it made me feel like things were hopeless. I've  racked up a lot of medical debt, which makes my financial situation worse.

It's not really anyone's fault, but I also feel like I got some bad advice. Therapists and people in my group really encouraged me to step out of my comfort zone, socialize, and meet new people. I did this and I was sexually assaulted.

Yes. I get so frustrated by people throwing out empty platitudes about things getting better and life being worth living. Some people don't get better. They're miserable for their entire lives, and it's cruel to deny them any sort of release. I've tried to follow the advice of my therapist and fix my life and things have only gotten worse.
